edges.mechanism: Omega-3s may reduce platelet aggregation/thromboxane A2 and factor VII; additive anticoagulant effect possible. No PK interaction: icosapent ethyl 4 g/d did not change R-/S-warfarin exposure or INR.
edges.evidence: Phase 1 PK/PD study (n=25, null); case report of INR 2.8->4.3 after fish oil doubled to 2 g/d; FDA labels advise periodic monitoring.

edges.mechanism: Additive effects on hemostasis; in REDUCE-IT bleeding with icosapent ethyl was greater with concomitant aspirin or clopidogrel.
edges.evidence: FDA Vascepa label (bleeding 12% vs 10%, serious 3% vs 2%); RCT MA: bleeding related to EPA dose, not background antiplatelet use.

edges.mechanism: Prolonged bleeding time (within normal limits) reported with omega-3s; labels advise monitoring with anticoagulants or other drugs affecting coagulation.
edges.evidence: FDA labels (Vascepa, Lovaza); MA of 11 RCTs: no overall bleeding excess (RR 1.09) but ~50% relative (0.6% absolute) increase with high-dose purified EPA.

edges.mechanism: Dose-dependent increase in incident AF (EPA-mediated in OMEMI; possibly vagal); more symptomatic recurrences in paroxysmal/persistent AF with Lovaza.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs: HR 1.25 overall, +11% per 1 g/d; OR 1.43 only at >1.5 g/d in high-CV-risk patients; FDA labels warn.

edges.mechanism: Products are derived from fish oil; residual fish protein could theoretically trigger reactions. Highly refined oils were tolerated in a small pilot challenge study; algal oil avoids fish source.
edges.evidence: FDA label warnings (Vascepa, Lovaza); pilot oral challenge study, 6/6 finned-fish-allergic patients tolerated fish oil.

edges.with: active bleeding or high bleeding risk
edges.mechanism: Antithrombotic effect of omega-3s; risk concentrated with high-dose purified EPA.
edges.evidence: RCT MA (n=120,643) and REDUCE-IT label data; absolute excess small.

edges.mechanism: Label recommends periodic ALT/AST monitoring in hepatic impairment during omega-3-acid ethyl ester therapy.
Omega-3 LCPUFA reduce preterm and early preterm birth but increase prolonged gestation (>42 wk) and possibly large-for-gestational-age infants; benefit mainly with low baseline status.
edges.evidence: Cochrane (26 RCTs): PTB RR 0.89, early PTB RR 0.58, prolonged gestation RR 1.61; ORIP null in replete women; ADORE dose effect in low-DHA women.

edges.mechanism: FADS1 insertion allele increases arachidonic acid synthesis; high-dose DHA reduced early preterm birth in I-carriers but increased prolonged gestation in D/D.
edges.evidence: Post hoc genotype analysis of ADORE RCT (n=761); needs prospective confirmation.

edges.mechanism: Positive EPA outcome trials were statin add-on; icosapent ethyl CV indication is adjunct to maximally tolerated statin.
edges.evidence: REDUCE-IT, JELIS, RESPECT-EPA; FDA Vascepa label.

edges.mechanism: Small additive blood-pressure lowering (about -2.6/-1.6 mmHg at 2-3 g/d).
Both listed as supplements that may interfere with hemostasis; stacking could add bleeding tendency.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; anecdotal cases only, controlled data insufficient.

edges.mechanism: Garlic and fish oil both reported to reduce platelet aggregation; theoretical additive bleeding risk.
Ginger and fish oil both proposed to affect hemostasis; theoretical additive bleeding risk.
Ginkgo and fish oil both proposed to affect platelet function; anecdotal hemorrhage reports with ginkgo.
No interaction on AF or depression in VITAL factorial; additive slowing of PhenoAge epigenetic clock with vitamin D and exercise in DO-HEALTH.
edges.evidence: Large factorial RCTs (VITAL, DO-HEALTH post hoc).

edges.mechanism: True physiological rise with DHA-containing products (DHA +7.23 mg/dL vs placebo; Lovaza +44.5% in severe HTG); EPA alone does not raise LDL-C.
edges.evidence: MA of monotherapy RCTs; EFSA opinion (~3% rise at 2-6 g/d); Lovaza label requires LDL monitoring.

edges.mechanism: Intended near-linear dose-dependent TG reduction via reduced hepatic VLDL-TG production.
edges.evidence: Dose-response MA of 90 RCTs; FDA labels.

edges.mechanism: RBC EPA+DHA (% of fatty acids) and EPA/AA ratio rise with supplementation; used as exposure/adherence markers and proposed risk targets (<4% vs >8%).
edges.evidence: Cohort-derived risk estimates; trial use of EPA/AA ratio; MA of 96 trials on blood fatty-acid response.
